title: Call an action from a button
summary: An action is a function stored alongside the values.
introduction: An action is a function stored alongside the values. Your task: Render the Count and Add components together.
learningObjectives: Render the Count and Add components together.
Explain the example for call an action from a button

blocks.text: An action is a function stored alongside the values. A component can select that function and call it after a click.
Use a React project with Zustand 5 installed. Hook examples belong in React components; vanilla examples use zustand/vanilla. These package imports require your own build tool.

blocks.code:
import {useReading} from "./store.js";
export default function Add(){const add=useReading(state=>state.add);return <button onClick={add}>Read one</button>;}
blocks.title: Call an action from a button

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: The hook selects the stored add function.
Passing that function to onClick waits for activation instead of calling it during rendering.

blocks.text: Clicking the button runs the store action and increases the count.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Pass the function to onClick. Writing onClick={add()} would call it while rendering.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Render the Count and Add components together.
